spots.name: Speicherstadt
spots.summary: The Speicherstadt in Hamburg, Germany, is the largest warehouse district in the world where the buildings stand on timber-pile foundations—oak logs, in this particular case. It is located in the port of Hamburg, in the HafenCity quarter, and was built from 1883 to 1927.

names.ja: シュパイヒャーシュタット

spots.name: Miniatur Wunderland
spots.summary: The Miniatur Wunderland is, according to Guinness World Records, the largest model railway system in the world. It is located at the historic Speicherstadt in Hamburg and is one of the most popular and most visited sights in Germany.

names.ja: ミニチュアワンダーランド

spots.name: St. Nicholas Church, Hamburg
spots.summary: The Church of St. Nicholas is a Gothic Revival cathedral that was formerly one of the five Lutheran Hauptkirchen in the city of Hamburg, Germany. The original chapel, a wooden building, was completed in 1195. It was replaced by a brick church in the 14th century, which was eventually destroyed by fire in 1842.

names.ja: 聖ニコライ教会

spots.name: Elbphilharmonie
spots.summary: The Elbphilharmonie, popularly nicknamed Elphi, is a concert hall in the HafenCity quarter of Hamburg, Germany, on the Grasbrook peninsula of the Elbe River.

names.ja: エルプフィルハーモニー・ハンブルク

spots.name: St. Michael's Church, Hamburg
spots.summary: St. Michael's Church, colloquially called Michel, is one of Hamburg's five Lutheran main churches (Hauptkirchen) and one of the most famous churches in the city. St. Michael is a landmark of the city and is considered one of the most important Protestant Baroque churches in northern Germany.

names.ja: 聖ミヒャエル教会

spots.name: Reeperbahn
spots.summary: The Reeperbahn is a street and entertainment district in Hamburg's St. Pauli district, one of the two centres of Hamburg's nightlife and also the city's major red-light district. In German, it is also nicknamed die sündige Meile and Kiez. The Reeperbahn Festival is among the largest club festivals.

names.ja: レーパーバーン

spots.name: Hamburger Kunsthalle

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Hamburger Kunsthalle is the art museum of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, Germany. It is one of the largest art museums in the country. It consists of three connected buildings, dating from 1869, 1921 (Kuppelsaal) and 1997, located in the Altstadt district between the Hauptbahnhof and the two Alster lakes.

names.ja: ハンブルク美術館

spots.name: Chilehaus
spots.summary: The Chilehaus is a ten-story office building in Hamburg, Germany in the Kontorhaus District. It is an example of the 1920s Brick Expressionism style of architecture. This large angular building is on a site of approximately 6,000 m2, spanning the Fischertwiete Street in Hamburg.

names.ja: チリハウス

spots.name: Hamburg City Hall
spots.summary: Hamburg City Hall is the seat of local government of Hamburg, Germany. It is the seat of the government of Hamburg and as such, the seat of one of Germany's 16 state parliaments.

names.ja: ハンブルク市庁舎

spots.name: Hamburg Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Hamburg Hauptbahnhof, or Hamburg Central Railway Station in English, is the main railway station of the city of Hamburg, Germany. Opened in 1906 to replace four separate terminal stations, today Hamburg Hauptbahnhof is operated by DB InfraGO AG.

names.ja: ハンブルク中央駅

spots.name: Tierpark Hagenbeck
spots.summary: The Tierpark Hagenbeck is a zoo in Stellingen, Hamburg, Germany. The collection began in 1863 with animals that belonged to Carl Hagenbeck Sr. (1810–1887), a fishmonger who became an amateur animal collector. The park itself was founded by Carl Hagenbeck Jr. in 1907.

names.ja: ハーゲンベック動物園

spots.name: Bismarck Monument
spots.summary: The Bismarck Monument in Hamburg is a memorial sculpture located in the St. Pauli quarter dedicated to Otto von Bismarck. It is one of 240 memorials to Bismarck worldwide and is the largest and probably best-known of these Bismarck towers.

spots.name: HafenCity
spots.summary: HafenCity is a quarter in the borough of Hamburg-Mitte, Hamburg, Germany. It is located on the Elbe river island Grasbrook, on the former Port of Hamburg area.

names.ja: ハーフェンシティ

spots.name: Elbe Tunnel
spots.summary: Old Elbe Tunnel or St. Pauli Elbe Tunnel, which opened in 1911, is a pedestrian and vehicle tunnel in Hamburg. The 426 m long tunnel was a technical sensation; 24 m beneath the surface, two 6 m diameter tubes connect central Hamburg with the docks and shipyards on the south side of the river Elbe.

names.ja: 旧エルベ・トンネル

spots.name: St. Pauli Piers
spots.summary: The St. Pauli Piers, is the largest landing site in the Port of Hamburg, Germany, and also one of Hamburg's major tourist attractions. Other English language translations include St. Pauli Landing Stages or St. Pauli Landing Bridges.

spots.name: Kontorhaus District
spots.summary: The Kontorhaus District is the southeastern part of Altstadt, Hamburg, between Steinstraße, Meßberg, Klosterwall and Brandstwiete. The streetscape is characterised by large office buildings in the style of Brick Expressionism of the early 20th century.

names.ja: コントーアハウス地区

spots.name: Flakturm IV
spots.summary: Right at the Heiligengeistfeld is a World War II bunker, visible from far away due to its size. Nowadays the building houses different media companies and agentures, and there's a dance club on the upper floor.

spots.name: Herbertstraße
spots.summary: Herbertstraße is a street in the St. Pauli district of Hamburg, located near the Reeperbahn, which is the main red-light district. It is the only street in the city where it is still possible to find prostitutes in windows as in the famous De Wallen district of Amsterdam.

names.ja: ヘルベルト通り

spots.name: Cap San Diego
spots.summary: MS Cap San Diego is a general cargo ship, situated as a museum ship in Hamburg, Germany.

spots.name: Al-Quds Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The al-Quds Mosque was a Sunni Islam mosque, located in Hamburg, Germany. The mosque was opened in 1993 and operated until 2010 when it was shut down by German security officials.

spots.name: Rickmer Rickmers
spots.summary: Rickmer Rickmers is a sailing ship permanently moored as a museum ship in Hamburg, near the Cap San Diego.

names.ja: リックマー・リックマーズ

spots.name: B-515
spots.summary: B-515 is a Tango-class submarine of the Soviet and Russian Navies. It remained in active service until 2001. It is currently docked in Hamburg and is open to the public as a museum exhibit. The submarine is sometimes referred to as U-434, which derives from the pennant number painted on the vessel.

spots.name: Heinrich Hertz Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Heinrich Hertz Tower is a landmark radio telecommunication tower in the city of Hamburg, Germany.

names.ja: ハインリヒ・ヘルツ塔

spots.name: Jungfernstieg
spots.summary: The Jungfernstieg is an urban promenade in Hamburg, Germany. It is the city's foremost boulevard.

names.ja: ユングフェルンシュティーク

spots.name: St. Peter’s Church
spots.summary: Saint Peter's Church in Hamburg, Germany stands on the site of many former cathedrals. It has been a Protestant cathedral since the Reformation and its congregation forms part of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in Northern Germany.

names.ja: 聖ペトリ中央教会

spots.name: Außenalster
spots.summary: Außenalster or Outer Alster Lake is the larger of the two artificial lakes formed by the Alster river in Hamburg, Germany, the other being the Binnenalster. The Außenalster and its shores are used by the inhabitants of Hamburg for many sport and recreational purposes, such as sailing and rowing.

spots.name: Köhlbrand Bridge
spots.summary: The Köhlbrand Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge in Hamburg, Germany, which connects the harbor area on the island of Wilhelmsburg between the Norderelbe and Süderelbe branches of the Elbe river with motorway 7. It bridges the Süderelbe, here called Köhlbrand, before it unites with the Norderelbe again.

spots.name: Altstadt, Hamburg
spots.summary: Altstadt, more precisely Hamburg-Altstadt is one of the inner-city districts of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, Germany.

names.ja: ハンブルク旧市街

spots.name: St. Mary's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Mary's Cathedral in Hamburg was the cathedral of the ancient Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hamburg, which was merged in personal union with the Diocese of Bremen in 847, and later in real union to form the Archdiocese of Hamburg-Bremen, as of 1027.

names.ja: ハンブルク大聖堂

photo.author: Peter Suhr (* 17. Juni 1788 in Hamburg, † 20. September 1857 ebenda)

spots.name: St. Catherine's Church, Hamburg

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Catherine's Church is one of the five principal Lutheran churches (Hauptkirchen) of Hamburg, Germany. The base of its spire, dating from the 13th century, is the second oldest building preserved in the city, after the lighthouse on Neuwerk island.

names.ja: 聖カタリーネン教会

spots.name: Hamburg State Opera
spots.summary: The Hamburg State Opera is an opera company based in Hamburg, Germany. Its theatre is near the square of Gänsemarkt. Since the 2025/26 season, the Intendant of the company is Tobias Kratzer, and the Generalmusikdirektor is Omer Meir Wellber.

names.ja: ハンブルク州立歌劇場

spots.name: Planten un Blomen
spots.summary: Planten un Blomen is an urban park with a size of 47 hectares in the inner-city of Hamburg, Germany. The name Planten un Blomen is Low German for "Plants and Flowers".

names.ja: プランテン・ウン・ブローメン

spots.name: Hygieia-Fountain
spots.summary: Between the buildings, there is a little courtyard called Rathaushof with its fountain, Hygieia-Brunnen.

names.fr: Fontaine à l'éfigie d'Hygie. Parvis de l'hôtel de ville de Hambourg (Allemagne)

photo.author: Hansueli Krapf This file was uploaded with Commonist.

spots.name: St. James' Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. James' Church is one of the five principal churches (Hauptkirchen) of Hamburg. In 1529, it became a Lutheran church. It is located directly in the city centre, has a 125 m-tall (410 ft) tower and features a famous organ by Arp Schnitger from 1693.

names.ja: 聖ヤコビ教会

spots.name: Dancing Towers

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dancing Towers are two highrises at the eastern end of Reeperbahn, in St. Pauli, Hamburg, Germany. Designed by BRT Architects of Hadi Teherani and funded by Strabag, they were completed in 2012.

spots.name: Hamburg Planetarium

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Hamburg Planetarium is one of the world's oldest, and one of Europe's most visited planetariums. It is located in the district of Winterhude, Hamburg, Germany, and housed in a former water tower at the center of Hamburg Stadtpark.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

names.ja: ハンマブルク城

spots.name: Rathausmarkt
spots.summary: Rathausmarkt is the central square of Hamburg, Germany, located in the Altstadt quarter right in front of the Hamburg Rathaus.

spots.name: Krameramtsstuben

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Krameramtsstuben are historic buildings on Krayenkamp, near St. Michaelis Church in the Neustadt district of Hamburg, Germany.

spots.name: Museum of Hamburg History

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Hamburg History is a history museum located in the city of Hamburg in northern Germany. The museum was established in 1908 and opened at its current location in 1922, although its parent organization was founded in 1839. The museum is located near the Planten un Blomen park in the center of Hamburg.

names.nl: Museum voor de geschiedenis van Hamburg
names.ja: ハンブルク歴史博物館

spots.name: Hamburg Stadtpark
spots.summary: Hamburg Stadtpark is a large urban park in the district of Winterhude, in the Hamburg borough of Hamburg-Nord. Spanning an area of 148 hectares, it is the second-largest park in the city after Altona Volkspark.

spots.name: Deichtorhallen

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Deichtorhallen in Hamburg, Germany, is one of Europe's largest art centers for contemporary art and photography.

spots.name: Bucerius Kunst Forum
spots.summary: The Bucerius Kunst Forum is an international exhibition centre in Hamburg, Germany, founded in 2002 through the ZEIT-Stiftung Ebelin und Gerd Bucerius foundation. It is named after Gerd Bucerius and his wife, and located directly beside the Hamburg Rathaus.

spots.name: Internationales Maritimes Museum Hamburg
spots.summary: The Internationales Maritimes Museum Hamburg is a private museum in the HafenCity quarter of Hamburg, Germany. The museum houses Peter Tamm's collection of model ships, construction plans, uniforms, and maritime art, amounting to over 40,000 items and more than one million photographs.

names.ja: ハンブルク国際海事博物館

spots.name: Mönckebergstraße
spots.summary: The Mönckebergstraße is one of the main shopping streets in Hamburg, Germany.

spots.name: Große Freiheit
spots.summary: The Große Freiheit is a street starting on the North Side to Hamburg's Reeperbahn road in the St. Pauli quarter. It is part of the red-light district.

spots.name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe Hamburg

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe Hamburg is a museum of fine, applied and decorative arts in Hamburg, Germany. It is located centrally, near the Hauptbahnhof.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe Hamburg

names.fr: Musée des arts et métiers de Hambourg
names.es: Museo de Artes y Oficios de Hamburgo
names.ja: ハンブルク美術工芸博物館

spots.name: Domkirche St. Marien

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Domkirche St. Marien is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Sankt Georg, Hamburg, Germany, and the metropolitan cathedral of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Hamburg. It was the first new Roman Catholic church built in Hamburg since the Reformation.

spots.name: Gänsemarkt
spots.summary: Gänsemarkt is a public square in Hamburg, Germany, located in the Neustadt quarter. The triangular urban square is accessible by streets of Jungfernstieg from the east, Dammtorstraße and Valentinskamp in the north west and ABC-Straße in the south.

spots.name: Rote Flora
spots.summary: The Rote Flora is a former theatre in the Sternschanze district of Hamburg, Germany. It has been squatted since November 1989 as a self-managed social centre. The collective said in 2001 "We are the 'UFO in the neighbourhood.' The black hole in public space.

spots.name: Hamburg Dungeon
spots.summary: Built in 2000, the Hamburg Dungeon is a tourist attraction from a chain including the London Dungeon and Berlin Dungeon. It is the first of this brand to be built in mainland Europe. It provides a journey through Hamburg’s dark history in an actor led, interactive experience.

names.ja: ハンブルク・ダンジョン

spots.name: Binnenalster
spots.summary: Binnenalster or Inner Alster Lake is the smaller of the two artificial lakes formed by the Alster river in Hamburg, Germany, the other being the Außenalster. The main annual festival is the Alstervergnügen.

spots.name: Hamburg Dammtor station
spots.summary: Hamburg Dammtor is a railway station for long distance, regional and suburban trains on the Hamburg-Altona link line, located in Central Hamburg, Germany. In front is a bus station of the same name for public transport.

names.ja: ハンブルク＝ダムトーア駅

spots.name: Deichstraße
spots.summary: Deichstraße is the oldest remaining street in the Altstadt of Hamburg, Germany and a popular visitor attraction in the city.

spots.name: SS Stettin
spots.summary: Stettin is a steam icebreaker built by the shipyard Stettiner Oderwerke in 1933. She was ordered by the Chamber of Commerce of Stettin. The economy of the city of Stettin strongly depended on the free access of ships to and from the Baltic Sea.

spots.name: Ohnsorg-Theater
spots.summary: The Ohnsorg-Theater in Hamburg, Germany, is a stage for plays run after the British system of repertory theatre with up to six produced plays per season. Plays are exclusively performed in Low German (Platt).

spots.name: Davidwache
spots.summary: The Davidwache is a police station in Hamburg, Germany. It is located in the St. Pauli quarter, near Reeperbahn, at the corner of Spielbudenplatz square and Davidstraße. Today, it is the seat of Hamburg Police Department 15.

spots.name: Dialogue in the Dark

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Dialogue in the Dark is an awareness raising exhibition and franchise, as well as a social business. In Dialogue in the Dark, blind guides lead visitors in small groups through different settings in absolute darkness.

names.ja: ダイアログ・イン・ザ・ダーク

spots.name: Chocoversum Hachez Schokoladen-Museum
spots.summary: The Chocoversum is a "museum" run by chocolate manufacturer Hachez from Hamburg's fellow Hansestadt Bremen. Rather than focus on exhibiting historic artifacts, it presents the process of making chocolate from the plantation up to the finished confection. There is also a studio where visitors can try their hands at being a chocolatier. 90-minute guided tours are provided everyday.

spots.name: Überseebrücke
spots.summary: This is where big cruise liners used to dock when coming to Hamburg.

spots.name: HafenCity Kesselhaus InfoCenter

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Here you can find information about the new buildings and the whole district. The InfoCenter also provides free guided tours.

spots.name: Feuerschiff LV 13
spots.summary: The big red lighthouse ship hosts a restaurant today.

spots.name: Aussichtspunkt Steinwerder
spots.summary: A viewing platform at the southern end of the Alter Elbtunnel, with great views on Landungsbrücken, the Elbphilharmonie, and Hamburg's harbourfront.

spots.name: Hopfenmarkt

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The hop market with its fountain Vierländerinbrunnen

spots.name: Zur Ritze

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Zur Ritze is fairly easy to find. It's near the Beatlesplatz at Reeperbahn; follow the signage down a small alley to the almost legendary door. The bar is almost always open, and it's a beautiful place to sit and talk all night. Having a nice night here won't break the bank, and it's a place to meet people who have made the Kiez the place it is today. The walls are full of photos, and in the basem

spots.name: Ristorante Borsalino

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Sternstraße 125, three minutes from S-Bahn station Sternschanze in the trendy neighbourhood of Schanzenviertel. Pizzas start from €6, fresh pasta is around €7-10 (try Pasta Mista), the meat dishes are delicious (it is right next to the "Schlachthof"-Slaughterhouse) and the four course menu is at €19.50. From 12:00-15:00 they serve a lunch menu for €6.50. Reservations recommended.

spots.name: St. Pauli Fischmarkt

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For Germans, it's a classic to eat bread with fish on St. Pauli Fischmarkt, especially very early in the Sunday morning (meaning 05:00 - 09:30) when visiting Hamburg. If for breakfast or as an after-party snack may depend on your inner clock, but if you are a fresh fish lover it is absolutely worth it since this fish was just fished during the night in Nordsee.

spots.name: ZaZa-Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small bar in a trendy neighbourhood that serves good drinks and has an interesting crowd of customers: some shoppers that celebrate their latest fashions, office workers that cool down, night owls that warm up, and quite few people who live in the area and just drop in for a drink. Has chairs outside. Happy Hour from 5PM-9PM and all night on Mondays.

spots.name: Cafe Paris
spots.summary: Classic French bistro in a beautiful historical building. Good place to get a coffee and pastry, or enjoy a leisurely lunch. Ground floor is very loud, crowded and busy. Upstairs (when entering turn right) is a quiet restaurant with a small bar (all food is also served at the bar). "Tartar" and "steak frites" can be strongly recommended.

spots.name: Der Etrusker

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun

spots.summary: Small and quite crowded Italian restaurant in the "Grindel" district near the university. Excellent Italian classics (pizza, pasta, etc.) for reasonable money. A lot of Italian restaurants as alternative to the left and right if you don't get a table. For dinner: make sure you are early (before 7pm) or make a reservation (only by phone).

spots.name: Shebeen
spots.summary: Cheap & cheerful bar with minimalist decoration celebrating St.Pauli FC and other friendly clubs. It's a hangout of the St.Pauli Ultras. Outsiders very welcome, but if you don't agree with what St.Pauli stands for, this is not the place to be. After matches it can get a bit rough if the competition decides to come visit.

spots.name: Delta Bistro

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Surprisingly cozy atmosphere. High quality meat and fish, but the menu offers some vegetarian dishes, too. Dishes are huge and the preparation quality comes close to star-awarded locations. It is advisable to reserve a table in advance, especially on Fridays and Saturdays in the autumn and winter months.

spots.name: Cafe Gnosa

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Coffeehouse with wide range of delicious self-made cakes and pastries. Famous for its cake buffet, also a great place to have breakfast or lunch. Gay-owned. Customers mixed by straight and gay people of any age. May not be easy to catch a table during rush-hours. For sugar- and caffeine-addicts.

spots.name: BPSchanzen1

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A tiny bar that houses many different DJs. The atmosphere is very friendly and good music is played. It's opposite the house that is occupied by various leftist fractions. (The yellow building with all the graffiti, named 'rote Flora'.)

spots.name: Kombüse
spots.summary: Mexican meets Hamburg punk/alternative. Excellent fresh ingredients. Vegan & veggie options (but also meat for the carnivores), with a huge range of hot sauces. Prices are low (€10.50 or less as of April 2015) and portions are huge.

spots.name: La Monella

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Hamburg's first vegetarian Italian restaurant. Small menu with Italian standards. Daily menu with dishes made of regional ingredients. Good place for a very delicious vegetarian lunch on a budget. Dinner slightly overpriced.

spots.name: Gun Club
spots.summary: Grungy but friendly punk bar in a cellar just off the Davidstraße. Came second in Hamburg Mexikanercontest (Mexikaner is a shot drink very similar to a bloody mary), and it shows - definitely the recommended drink here.

spots.name: McBoat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The only McDonald's that you can order your meal (on its app) and have it delivered to the shores while paddling along the canal. The meal is prepared fresh in the restaurant right next to the shoreline.

spots.name: Uebel und Gefährlich

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In a former bunker from World War II, it can be found near St. Pauli in Feldstraße. Easy to reach with the metro U3. Music used to be more hard house and electro but is changing nowadays from day to day.

spots.name: Washington-Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Relaxed bar covered in Hunter S. Thompson quotes with atmosphere to match. Small dance floor with DJ who plays everything from psychedelic jazz to German hip-hop. Excellent selection of gin&tonics.

spots.name: Alster Cliff

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nice place to stop for coffee and cake or a meal with a good view on the Alster lake. Lunch food (salad, pizza, pasta) are of average quality and above average price.

spots.name: Lokmam

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: It is not without reason that a lot of Turkish people love this place. Take the S11/S31 subway and get out at Sternschanze. From there Lokmam is seven minutes away.

spots.name: Fischereihafen-Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Große Elbstraße 143. Excellent view of parts of the port and the river Elbe. Many celebs have dined here, including English royals.

spots.name: Feldstern

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cozy pub/restaurant with affordable German food and outside seating in the summer. Nice lunch menu from 12:00-16:00 on weekdays.
